R6I-deer-walk-0006.name: 3.8 km NW of Mill Creek
R6I-deer-walk-0006.pressureWhy: 3.4 km on foot from the nearest parking (estimate).
R6I-deer-walk-0006.parkWhat: pull off on Mill Lk/Duece/Mike (gravel road)

evidence.t: No official deer winter range within 500 m, so the top score here is 8 of 11. This score leans on cutblocks, burns, habitat zone and aspect.
Cutblock harvested 2018 (8 years old), right here.
Burn from 2018 (fire R42356, 357 ha), right here.
Habitat zone Coastal Western Hemlock (CWHws2): coast forest, where black tailed deer are among the most common large mammals (95%) and use logged ground often (80%) (lesson: Wet forests).
S facing slope, 15 degrees: sun melts snow first.
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).

plan: Drive: from City of Terrace, about 117 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 55.20462, -128.05805, pull off on Mill Lk/Duece/Mike (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 3.4 km W, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 404 m, about 109 min at 3 km/h.
Hunt: deer, Sept, Oct, Nov, Dec (season rows). Watch the edge of the 2018 cutblock (right here) at first and last light. Sit above it with the wind in your face and glass (Tip).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 165 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 6-15, Region 6. Season: mule deer bucks Sept 10 to Nov 30 and more rows (synopsis page 50, 99%). 1 legal flag below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-01, closures 2026-10-16.
R6I-deer-walk-0006.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 6-15: about 328 hunter days a year for mule deer and white tailed deer (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.04 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: a long walk from parking. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

evidence.t: 3 wetlands within 2 km; nearest 4.6 ha, right here.

flags.t: Route crosses reserve land: GITANYOW 2. Get permission from the band office to hunt on or across it (synopsis page 9, 99%).

seasonRows.notes: MU 6-15 is not listed in the Region 6 moose rows (my reading of the table).

plan: Drive: from City of Terrace, about 114 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Beam Station Rd, Queensway Dr, Hwy 16 and 37, Hwy 37.
Park: 55.17525, -128.02874, pull off on Hwy 37 (paved road). Map links below.
Walk: 5.2 km W, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 260 m, about 130 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 100 m E of the spot at 440 m (55.15799, -128.10264). Water: unnamed wetland right here (estimate).
Hunt: moose, season: VERIFY. Glass the wetland and cutblock edges at dawn and dusk. Move slowly, stop often (Tip).
Use: .308 Winchester, 165 to 180 grain premium bullet, shots inside about 200 m (219 yd) (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 6-15, Region 6. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-01, closures 2026-10-16.
